title: Decomposing Any Function into Even and Odd Parts
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Show how any function f defined on a symmetric domain can be written as the sum of an even function and an odd function, and decompose f(x) = x^2 + x as an illustration.
finalAnswer: $f(x) = \underbrace{\tfrac{f(x)+f(-x)}{2}}_{\text{even part}} + \underbrace{\tfrac{f(x)-f(-x)}{2}}_{\text{odd part}}$; for $f(x) = x^2 + x$ this gives even part $x^2$ and odd part $x$.

steps.title: Set Up the Two Candidates
steps.explanation: The domain must be symmetric about 0 so that f(-x) exists whenever f(x) does. Adding E and O reconstructs f immediately, since the f(-x) terms cancel: E(x) + O(x) = f(x).
steps.why: Construction plus a one-line check of the sum proves existence at once.

steps.title: Verify the Parities
steps.explanation: Swapping x for -x in E merely reorders the sum, so E is even. In O the swap flips the sign of every term, so O is odd. Thus f really is a sum of an even and an odd function.
steps.why: Definition-by-definition verification is the expected proof style for this review question.

steps.title: Note Uniqueness and Compute an Example
steps.mathExpression: f = E + O \implies x^2 + x = x^2 + x
steps.explanation: The decomposition is unique: if f = g + h with g even and h odd, then g - E = H - h is simultaneously even and odd, hence zero. For f(x) = x^2 + x: f(-x) = x^2 - x, so E = ((x^2+x)+(x^2-x))/2 = x^2 and O = ((x^2+x)-(x^2-x))/2 = x.
steps.why: Uniqueness explains why even and odd parts are regarded as intrinsic features of f, not arbitrary choices.
